# Mailroom-ML: appendix {.page-title}

[M9c supporting tables · evaluation protocol, gates, per-head results]{.kicker}

These tables support the [Mailroom-ML case study](../mailroom-ml.qmd). Every number below comes from the held-out test report for run `m9c-20261014-113614`, or from the trainer configuration recorded in it. They are copied, not re-run here.

## Evaluation protocol

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Run tag | `m9c-20261014-113614` |
| Model | `answerdotai/ModernBERT-base`, hierarchical heads |
| Documents | 323 held-out test documents |
| Windows | 541 (8,192 tokens, 512-token overlap) |
| Seed | 42 |
| Reported by | `training/eval/eval_modernbert.py`, `--subset test --sample 0` |

Training configuration for this arm: 6 epochs, batch 8 with gradient accumulation 4, learning rate 2e-5, subclass-head learning rate 1e-3, document-type loss weight 0.5, logit adjustment 0.5, label smoothing 0.05, warmup fraction 0.06.

## Headline metrics

| Metric | Value | Denominator |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Document-type accuracy | 0.9598 | 310 of 323 |
| Conditional subclass accuracy | 0.7387 | 229 of 310 scorable |
| Window calibration ECE | 0.0189 | 541 windows |
| Window band ECE | 0.0659 | 541 windows |
| Confidence-only acceptance | 0.3901 | 126 of 323 |
| OOD flag rate | 0.0557 | 18 of 323 |
| Latency | 0.573 s per document | One NVIDIA L4 GPU |

The calibration figure is a window-level ECE, not a document-level probability check. The acceptance figure is confidence-only; it omits the support, catch-all, head-exclusion and subclass-projection guards, so the full gate can accept fewer documents.

## Release gates

| Gate | Actual | Threshold | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Contract test macro-F1 | 0.3589 | ≥ 0.20 | Met |
| Correspondence test macro-F1 | 0.5249 | ≥ 0.25 | Met |
| Document-type test accuracy | 0.9598 | ≥ 0.89 | Met |
| Window ECE, document type | 0.0189 | ≤ 0.05 | Met |

Two report-only targets sit outside that gate set. Document-type accuracy clears 0.95 (0.9598). Conditional subclass accuracy does not reach 0.75 (0.7387), so passing the release gates is not a blanket subclass-quality claim.

## Per-head results

| Head | Test macro-F1 |
| --- | ---: |
| Insurance claim | 1.0000 |
| Corporate record | 0.7733 |
| Correspondence | 0.5249 |
| Contract | 0.3589 |
| Merger agreement | 0.1774 |

Insurance claims are a near-balanced, highly templated control head, so 1.0000 is not general skill. Merger agreement remains the weakest head.

Calibrated ECE by head, from checkpoint selection on the **validation** split rather than the test split:

| Head | Calibrated ECE (validation) |
| --- | ---: |
| Insurance claim | 0.0000 |
| Document type | 0.0163 |
| Merger agreement | 0.0402 |
| Corporate record | 0.0465 |
| Contract | 0.0552 |
| Correspondence | 0.1045 |

## Cohorts and selective risk

| Cohort | Documents | Document-type accuracy | Mean window agreement | Window ECE |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Single-window | 274 | 0.9599 | 1.0000 | 0.0259 |
| Multi-window | 49 | 0.9592 | 0.9799 | 0.0163 |

The global selective-risk sweep reports its error budget as met at a 0.94 threshold, with coverage of about 0.843 at that pick. The multi-window cohort alone does **not** meet the budget and returns no threshold. Both figures come from the same test pool used for other checks, so treat them as diagnostics, not as independently validated deployment thresholds.

| Document type | Documents |

## Scope

::: {.caveat}
**One checkpoint, one test pool.** These tables describe a single release, not a production service level. The test split informed run comparisons, the selective-risk sweep and the decode sweep, so the coverage figures are optimistic. Contract and correspondence stay off the fast path by checkpoint policy.
:::
